name: after_update_audit
comment: The fixture trigger (ADR-0042): one neutral body, three renderings. {new: cols} is the changed rows as a relation (inserted on SQL Server, a one-row derived table over new. elsewhere); {now} the UTC time in the storage form; the wrapper — begin/end, set nocount on, the PostgreSQL function and its return null — is the dialect's. The drop is idempotent and takes what the dialect created beside the trigger.

trigger.name: trg_roles_audit

create:
create trigger trg_roles_audit after update on roles for each row
begin
insert into role_changes (role_id, role_name, changed_at)
select n.id, n.role_name, strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')
from (select new.id as id, new.role_name as role_name) n;
end

create trigger [trg_roles_audit] on [roles] after update as
begin
    set nocount on;
insert into role_changes (role_id, role_name, changed_at)
select n.id, n.role_name, todatetimeoffset(sysutcdatetime(), 0)
from inserted n;
end
drop: if object_id(N'trg_roles_audit', N'TR') is not null drop trigger [trg_roles_audit]

create:
create or replace function "trg_roles_audit_fn"() returns trigger language plpgsql as $$
begin
insert into role_changes (role_id, role_name, changed_at)
select n.id, n.role_name, now()
from (select new."id" as "id", new."role_name" as "role_name") n;
    return null;
end
$$
create trigger "trg_roles_audit" after update on "roles" for each row execute function "trg_roles_audit_fn"()
